audit.title: Using Data Feeds on Starknet

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Good. The intro leads with a clean claim: "Chainlink Data Feeds are available on Starknet Sepolia as Cairo smart contracts." Section leads are self-contained. Weakness: the page's implied question ("how do I read a feed on Starknet?") is answered only after a Starknet primer; a one-line "to read a feed, call `latest_round_data` on the proxy" near the top would win more lifts.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Good hierarchy, but the measured **1 level skip** (H1 → H3 for "Offchain/Onchain/Devnet examples") breaks the outline; those should be H2. Sections are appropriately sized (median 52 words, max 241). Only 1 table, 0 bullets — the three "examples" subsections would scan better as a comparison table or list.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Code and table carry real specifics (proxy address, `0.2.8` version, decoded round data), but **prose has only 1 numeral in 543 words**. No feed decimals, heartbeat/deviation thresholds, or supported-network count in text.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 15 links, 4 to primary GitHub sources (Starkli, cairo-lang, starknet-foundry, devnet-rs) plus Cairo language docs. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good crisp definitions: "Starknet is a permissionless decentralized Zk-rollup operating as an L2 network over Ethereum" and the Starkli description. Could add a one-liner defining `latest_round_data` output fields as a set.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured: **0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, datePublished/dateModified absent, 0 og/twitter tags.** No freshness or `TechArticle` schema for engines to trust. Head metadata could not be verified from the captured content; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a definitive read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; all 3 fences tagged `bash`, commands include the full address, selector, and a live RPC endpoint, and expected output is shown. No imports needed for CLI. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Moderate. Covers setup → read across offchain/onchain/devnet, but no troubleshooting/FAQ and no symptom-phrased entries (RPC errors, version mismatch, EVM-incompatibility surprises). Devs querying by error string won't retrieve this page.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent naming (Starknet Sepolia, Starkli, Cairo), unambiguous prose. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a compact, well-written tutorial for reading Chainlink Data Feeds on Starknet Sepolia via the Starkli CLI, with a strong worked example (real proxy address, runnable command, decoded output table). Its biggest GEO strength is a copy-pasteable, fully-specified `starkli call` example plus a hex→decimal decoding table an engine can lift directly. Its biggest opportunity is machine-readability metadata — the served page carries no JSON-LD, canonical URL, or last-updated signal — closely followed by missing symptom/error-phrased query coverage. Honest verdict: solid content that under-signals its trustworthiness and freshness to parsers, and leaves common failure-mode queries uncovered.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and visible last-updated
recommendations.issue: measured "JSON-LD: 0 block(s) … canonical: MISSING … dateModified absent"
recommendations.change: emit a `TechArticle` JSON-LD block with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: Cairo`, and a self-referential `canonical`; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: freshness and schema are direct E-E-A-T/trust signals that raise citation rate and let agents parse the page reliably.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom/error-phrased troubleshooting section
recommendations.where: new H2 after "Read data from a Chainlink Price Feed"
recommendations.change: add Q-phrased subheads: "starkli: command not found", "Invalid selector / function not found", "Why isn't Starknet EVM-compatible?", "RPC endpoint returns error". Each with a one-line fix.
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by error string; symptom-titled headings win retrieval that concept prose loses.

recommendations.title: Lead with the canonical read action
recommendations.issue: opens with Starknet primer before the task
recommendations.change: add a first liftable sentence: "To read a Chainlink Data Feed on Starknet Sepolia, call `latest_round_data` on the feed's proxy aggregator address using the Starkli CLI."
recommendations.why: puts the canonical API in the first liftable sentence, resisting generic-EVM parametric priors (e.g. Solidity `latestRoundData`).

recommendations.title: Fix the heading level skip
recommendations.change: promote these to H2, or nest them under an H2 "Read data feeds off-chain and on-chain".
recommendations.why: clean hierarchy improves chunk-boundary detection for RAG.

recommendations.title: Add feed decimals / decoding note to prose
recommendations.change: state "ETH/USD uses 8 decimals, so `354661371569` = $3,546.61," and note where to find each feed's decimals.
recommendations.why: quantitative specifics with units are high-lift and answer a common follow-up query.

recommendations.title: Convert the three example types into a decision table
recommendations.issue: parallel prose blocks, no structured comparison (0 bullets)
recommendations.change: a small table — Method | Needs account? | Tooling | When to use — for offchain / onchain / devnet.
recommendations.why: lets engines extract *reasons* and build a justified "which should I use" answer.

antiPatterns: Undated content — no visible publish/modified date (measured absent); risks looking stale.
No wall-of-text, keyword stuffing, or marketing fluff detected. Cross-references are all resolved links.
offPageNotes: The page already references `/llms.txt`; confirm this URL is listed there so agents discover it.
Site-level JSON-LD/schema injection and freshness cadence are template/CI concerns beyond this single page.
Head metadata was not captured in the provided content — pass raw `<head>` in the CLI to verify canonical/og tags rather than assume absence.
